Just now

In Part 3 of our series, we built a highly scalable, disk-persistent vector search engine using Facebook AI Similarity Search (FAISS) and HNSW graphs. We successfully queried our index and returned a structured payload of relevant documents, metadata, and confidence scores in milliseconds.
But now we face the ultimate bottleneck of any Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) system: the LLM context window.
Press enter or click to view image in full size

Many developers think prompt engineering is just a matter of string concatenation. They find their top matches, dump them into a generic f-string, and hope the model figures it out:
# The common RAG anti-pattern: Naive Concatenation
prompt = f"Answer the query: {query}\n\nContext:\n" + "\n".join([doc['text'] for doc in retrieved_docs])In a production environment, this naive approach is a ticking time bomb. It ignores token budgets, exposes you to prompt injection vulnerabilities, and falls prey to a critical transformer attention bias known as the “Lost in the Middle” phenomenon.
In this guide, we will use Cursor to write a production-grade context-packing pipeline that formats, budget-checks, and strategically orders our FAISS results to construct a flawless, high-efficiency prompt.
